referents.why: Second masculine singular 'you' in the psalm's own voice; the speech turns from the third person of verse 1 to address the LORD named there. No other candidate is a second person.
First common singular 'me' in the psalm's own voice; the psalm is not quoting anyone.
Second masculine singular possessive on 'rod' (your rod): the rod belongs to the addressee of the speech, the LORD.
Second masculine singular possessive on 'staff' (your staff): same addressee as the rod.
Third masculine plural 'they' takes the rod and staff together as its referent, the only composite candidate that can take a plural; a single one of the two does not fit the plural.
referents.category: plural pronoun for a pair of objects

referents.why: First common singular 'me' as object of comfort, the psalm's own voice.
Implied first common singular subject of the yiqtol 'I will go'; the psalm's own voice.
Implied first common singular subject of the yiqtol 'I will fear'; the psalm's own voice.

links.why: cl2 opens with כִּי, 'for', and gives the reason for not fearing evil; the edge runs from what is explained to its reason.
'conceded' is not among the link_types; the concession is the 'though' type, added below.
cl0 opens with גַּם כִּי, 'even though', and cl1 is the claim that holds anyway: 'I will not fear, even though I walk through the valley'.

After 'you are with me', the rod and staff clause and 'they comfort me' give how the LORD is with him, the detail of the earlier clause. Whether it is detail or a new assertion is recorded in cant_tell.

groups.why: The even-though clause cl0, the claim that holds anyway cl1, and its ground cl2 (for you are with me) form the concession kind. builder_groups was empty.

none_fit.what: A fronted nominal phrase that is the subject of cl4, a left-dislocated topic before its predicate. No link type or group kind marks a topic.

cant_tell.what: Whether cl3-cl4 (rod and staff, they comfort me) is the detail of cl2 or a separate assertion
cant_tell.why: The clauses are joined by no conjunction, so the form does not decide. Recorded as elaborates above, which may be wrong.
